decideTranslation(analysis) is a pure function with SKIP_RATIO = 0.97 / CONFIRM_RATIO = 0.7: totalChars === 0 or ratio >= 0.97 => skip (reason empty / target-language, percent for display), ratio >= 0.70 => confirm with percent, otherwise translate-all; boundaries use raw ratio with >= semantics while the displayed percent is rounded
scope="non-target" keeps every target-language block byte-identical, replaces only non-target blocks and leaves order and structure unchanged

features.scope: Construction detail lives in `docs/features/default-save-path/FSD.md` plus stage documents S1-settings-and-ipc.md, S2-download-flow.md and S3-release.md. The settings contract gains a root-level `output: { defaultPath: string | null, useDefaultPath: boolean }` (SETTINGS_VERSION stays 1; a missing `output` is read leniently as the default - the only sanctioned relaxation of strict validation, so old settings.json files never trigger the corrupt-backup reset); the Electron main process gains two IPC channels (`md-convertor:output:select-directory`, `md-convertor:output:save-file`) behind `window.mdConvertor.output`, with path-traversal and filename validation enforced in both preload and main; the settings page gains an Output card (read-only path display, choose-directory button, use-default toggle); the home page download branches three ways - bridge + toggle on + path set: write directly and show a saved-path notice, bridge save fails: degrade to the browser download with a notice, anything else: the unchanged 0.3.5 browser download. Non-goals: no per-file prompt mode, no save dialog anywhere in the new path, no file-history or multi-directory rotation, no web-behaviour change.
nonGoals: No conversion-pipeline, translation-engine or scraping-security changes
No `dialog.showSaveDialog` - the toggle replaces the prompt, it does not re-skin it
No automatic recovery beyond one `mkdir -p`; an unwritable directory degrades to the browser download with a notice
No history, recent files, or duplicate-name suffixing (same-name files are overwritten, matching the browser save-as semantics)

S2 decision record (2026-09-22): the S2 spec claimed `EACCES -> 没有写入权限` and `ENOENT -> 目录不存在`, but S1 shipped only business codes (INVALID_DIR_PATH / INVALID_FILENAME / INVALID_CONTENT / CANCELLED / OUTPUT_SAVE_FAILED / IPC_FAILED) while electron/output.mjs returns the raw `error.code ?? "OUTPUT_SAVE_FAILED"`. Resolved as option (a) - add the real filesystem codes - and rejected option (b) (soften the doc). Rationale: the notice is the only place that explains why the direct write was skipped after the download already degraded, so a generic string throws that information away; normalising codes in the main process would push presentation into the IPC contract; and the fix is a pure string-table addition with no contract, IPC or version change. EACCES, EPERM, ENOENT, ENOTDIR, ENOSPC and EROFS were added. Two deliberate deviations, both commented in code and written up in the S2 doc: (1) the six extra codes beyond the two the spec named, EPERM because macOS returns it in some sandbox paths; (2) the failure sentence uses a colon instead of the spec's parentheses (`直接保存失败：{reason}已改为浏览器下载。`) because every mapped message is already a full sentence ending in a period - the settings page renders them verbatim - and `（没有写入权限。）` nests punctuation; the e2e assertions match substrings and are insensitive to the connector

ROOT CAUSE 1: `isAbsoluteDirPath` in electron/preload-contract.cjs (and its byte-equivalent copy in electron/preload.cjs) rejected ANY path containing `~`, not just a leading home shorthand - and the directory the user picked is `/Users/huanghaohai/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Note/未归档`, so every iCloud Drive folder was unusable. S2 T2.7 environment finding (2026-09-22): `CODEBUDDY_BROKER_DENY` is injected-sandbox noise, and it has a switch. WorkBuddy passes `NODE_OPTIONS=--require=".../cli/vendor/shim/node-language-shim.cjs"` to every node child; that shim conditionally loads `node-brokered-fs-shim.cjs`, which rewrites `mkdirSync/renameSync/copyFileSync/cpSync/chmodSync` to go through a broker file-token approval and throws errors coded `CODEBUDDY_BROKER_DENY` when refused. Its first statement is `if (!BROKERED_FS_HOOK_ENABLED) return;` with `BROKERED_FS_HOOK_ENABLED = process.env.CODEBUDDY_BROKERED_FS_HOOK_ENABLED === '1' || process.env.CODEBUDDY_SAFE_DELETE_SANDBOX === '1'` plus a required session id, so clearing `NODE_OPTIONS` for the command stops the shim loading entirely and gives native fs semantics. Consequence for this repository: any test asserting a real errno (ENOTDIR/EPERM/EACCES) must be run as `NODE_OPTIONS= npx vitest run <file>` or `NODE_OPTIONS= ./init.sh` in this agent environment, otherwise a legitimate assertion failure and a sandbox refusal look the same. S2 T2.8 environment trap (2026-09-22): `MD_CONVERTOR_USER_DATA` CANNOT isolate the packaged app. `electron/env.mjs` `buildServerEnv()` sets `MD_CONVERTOR_USER_DATA: userDataDir` unconditionally - the comment above it says the MD_CONVERTOR_* keys are always authoritative - so the main process's own userData path always wins and setting the variable before launching the app does nothing. Consequence: EVERY real-machine probe of this app reads and writes the user's real `settings.json` and drops its output file into whatever directory the switch currently points at. The T2.8 probe hit exactly that (the attempted isolation silently failed, the app read the real settings and wrote into the real iCloud directory). A probe must therefore back up the real settings.json, diff every field except `output` afterwards to prove nothing else moved (the page's PUT replaces the whole object), restore `defaultPath`/`useDefaultPath`, and delete the file it dropped in the real target directory. All four steps were run for T2.8 and the user's settings.json and iCloud directory are back to their pre-probe state
